mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover from the latest dip, commuting traffic will convert into more weekday shopping trips and raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace attendance stays depressed or if transit remains weak despite any short-lived retail rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -18.6 at t-0w after -33.4 at t-1w; TRANSIT was still -2.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 4 weeks even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run substitution away from retail is indicated when RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and RETAIL_REC stays below baseline; this pattern predicts another four weeks of muted retail mobility as households continue staying in. The mechanism fails if RESIDENTIAL falls back while RETAIL_REC remains flat or rises.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive at 5.0 in t-0w while RETAIL_REC stayed negative at -13.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above baseline in each of the next four weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent elevated level reflects concentrated essential trips that substitute for discretionary shopping and suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The effect fails if grocery mobility falls but retail mobility still does not recover.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays at least 20 points above baseline for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 22.4 to 30.1 across the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above 20 points above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls sharply while WORKPLACES also weaken, access costs rise and discretionary retail visits decline within one week. This mechanism fails if transit recovers or if retail rises despite a concurrent commute slowdown.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops more than 5 points week-on-week after being near baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -1.0 at t-2w to -10.7 at t-1w, then -2.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next weekly mean after a transit drop exceeding 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual recovery in PARKS from a very negative base signals improved outdoor conditions and broader willingness to leave home, which then lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks. The hypothesis fails if parks mobility improves but retail remains stuck below the prior four-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained negative but moved from -25.4 at t-1w to -21.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite a sustained week-over-week rise in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES from the sharp t-1w slump to a less negative level at t-0w should spill over into nearby retail demand with a two-week lag. The effect fails if workplace mobility rebounds but retail spending locations do not follow.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises at least 10 points week-on-week from a trough
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES changed from -33.4 at t-1w to -18.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean two weeks after WORKPLACES improves by at least 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while TRANSIT falls, people are substituting home-based activity for outside discretionary trips, which pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if both indicators move in the same direction or if retail improves despite the stay-at-home pattern.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was positive in all four weeks while TRANSIT stayed near or below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and TRANSIT stays below baseline in the same weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A regime of reopening after mobility suppression makes retail the last category to normalize; once both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES exceed their recent averages, retail should turn up within four weeks. The hypothesis fails if the commute recovery does not translate into retail recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both move above their 4-week means
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below baseline in the snapshot, with recent volatility
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES cross above their four-week averages.
